questions.question: Under START, a patient who walks to the designated area is tagged:
questions.rationale: Ambulatory patients are tagged Minor (green) and re-triaged later.

questions.question: A non-ambulatory adult has RR 32, radial pulse present, follows commands. START category:
A non-ambulatory adult has RR 30, radial pulse present, CRT 1 s, follows commands. START category:
questions.rationale: The criterion is MORE than 30; 30 passes. Perfusion and mental status are normal → Delayed.

questions.question: An adult is apneic. After you reposition the airway, he begins breathing. Tag:
questions.rationale: Breathing only after airway positioning → Immediate.

questions.question: An adult has RR 18, absent radial pulse. Tag:
An adult has RR 16, strong radial pulse, but cannot follow simple commands. Tag:
questions.rationale: Altered mental status (can't follow commands) → Immediate.

questions.question: JumpSTART: a 4-year-old is apneic after airway positioning but has a palpable pulse. Next step:
options: A. Give 5 rescue breaths and reassess
questions.rationale: 5 rescue breaths; if breathing resumes → Immediate; if not → Deceased.

questions.question: JumpSTART: a 6-year-old has RR 30, palpable peripheral pulse, alert, deformed femur, can't walk. Tag:
JumpSTART: a 5-year-old responds to pain only with abnormal flexion (posturing). Tag:
Which is NOT performed during START primary triage?
options: D. Asking the patient to follow a command
questions.rationale: CPR is not performed during mass-casualty triage.

questions.question: A night-time winter MCI. The best START perfusion check is:
questions.rationale: Cold and darkness make CRT unreliable — use the radial pulse.
